skeptic_materiality.round1: refuted=True, major: Opened PFE:10q_2026Q2.md p.37 and p.5, PFE:10k_FY2025.md p.43 (printed 37) and p.58. Every input line is on page and the reader's ratios reproduce: 2024 33,888/(53,816+33,888)=38.6%; 2025 36,374/88,037=41.3%; H1'25 16,569/39,817=41.6%; H1'26 17,280/40,858=42.3%. But the H1 2026 widening is not 'led by chargebacks'. Line by line H1'26 vs H1'25: chargebacks +639, but Medicare rebates -207 and sales allowances -142 offset most of it; sales returns and cash discounts +280 (919 vs 639). Excluding returns/cash discounts the rate is flat: (17,280-919)/40,858=40.04% vs (16,569-639)/39,817=40.01%. So the whole 0.68-pt H1 widening is the returns line, which p.38 ties at least partly to Comirnaty ('a lower favorable adjustment to the returns provision') and Nurtec ('higher returns'), i.e., lumpy, not a run-rate. The '$0.5-0.6B/yr, ~$0.10 pre-tax EPS ongoing' estimate annualizes a non-recurring returns swing and is unsupported. The 2025 step-up (+2.7 pts) is real arithmetic but the denominator lost ~$3.3B of Paxlovid and ~$1.1B of Comirnaty (10-K p.43 revenue bridge), so mix inflates it; the reader concedes this. Also the deduction table covers all gross product revenue (U.S. and international), so the ratio is a blended proxy, not a U.S. GTN rate. Correction: 2025 deductions rose to 41.3% of gross product sales from 38.6% (partly COVID mix). In H1 2026 the ex-returns deduction rate was flat at ~40.0%; the headline widening to 42.3% came from returns/cash discounts (+$280M), with chargebacks up $639M but offset by lower Medicare rebates and sales allowances. No supported ongoing GTN drag estimate.
skeptic_materiality.round2: refuted=True, major. Conceded: The 2025 38.6% to 41.3% step should be dropped, because it was guided on the 2024Q4 call (verified p.7). The reader's own footnote also attributes part of 2025 to the Paxlovid/Comirnaty commercial transition. The H1 2026 widening (41.6% to 42.3%), Q2 chargebacks +11.8% and returns +95% appear only in the 10-Q MD&A deduction table (10-Q 2026Q2 p37), not in the earnings release. The verified analyst_topics table shows gross_to_net_price asked 0 times on the 2025Q1-2026Q1 calls and once in 2026Q2, and that one turn (Tewari) was about 340B and CDK4, not Pfizer's deduction rate (market/priced_in_scorecard.csv, gross_to_net_price row). Correction: Drop the 2025 38.6%->41.3% step as evidence, since it was guided (~$1B Part D headwind) and partly COVID mix. Keep the claim that in H1 2026 deductions widened again (~0.7 pt), led by chargebacks and returns that no analyst has asked about. It becomes clearly non-obvious only if shown to exceed peers' 2026 deduction trend.
skeptic_obviousness.round2: refuted=True, major. skeptic_materiality.round1: refuted=False, minor: Opened PFE:10q_2026Q2.md p.38, ALNY:10q_2026Q2.md p.38, BBIO:10q_2026Q2.md p.56. All three figures are on page, same calendar quarter (PFE quarter ends June 28, rivals June 30, immaterial), all USD, units converted correctly (ALNY/BBIO in thousands). Vyndaqel family U.S. 1,064 vs 990; Amvuttra United States 809,079 vs 361,346 (a U.S.-only row, not global); BBIO net product revenue 222,440 vs 71,501, which p.56 attributes to Attruby, and BBIO commercializes only in the U.S. (ex-U.S. Beyonttra comes in as royalty revenue, a separate line), so it is effectively U.S. Arithmetic re-done: 1,064+809.1+222.4=2,095.5, share 50.8%; 990+361.3+71.5=1,422.8, share 69.6%; -18.8 pts. H1 U.S. 1,975 vs 1,976 and the 159M H1 shortfall vs 8% FY2025 growth (PFE:10k_FY2025.md p.44: 3,834 vs 3,547) also check. Weaknesses are definitional, not arithmetic: (1) it is revenue share, not patient share, and Amvuttra carries a much higher per-patient price, so revenue share overstates rival patient share; (2) Amvuttra U.S. includes hATTR-PN in both periods, and its ATTR-CM label was new in the base quarter, so the year-ago rival base is a launch-curve trough; (3) Vyndaqel's own revenue share loss partly reflects its own net price cuts (p.38 'net price erosion ... new payer contracts'), not only lost patients; (4) the latest quarter shows U.S. Vyndaqel +7%, so the stall is H1, not Q2. Materiality passes: $0.3B/yr shortfall is ~0.5% of $62.6B revenue, but the 10-pt sensitivity (~$0.8B, ~1.3%) and Vyndaqel's ~10% of revenue ($6,380M, 10-K p.44) clear the bar. Correction: Say 'U.S. ATTR-CM-class revenue share (approximate; Amvuttra U.S. includes hATTR-PN; revenue not patients)' fell from ~70% to ~51% Q2'25 to Q2'26, with Vyndaqel U.S. flat in H1 2026 despite +7% in Q2; part of the share loss is Pfizer's own payer-contract price cuts.
skeptic_materiality.round2: refuted=False, minor. Conceded: Share loss and its causes (first-line share to Attruby, payer contracting) were said on the 2025Q2 and 2025Q3 calls, and rivals publish share forecasts. The existence of share loss is not new. Held: The quantification is material and unsaid. Vyndaqel took ~0 of $1.25B of H1 U.S. class growth on a ~$3.8B U.S. product, and no Pfizer source sizes it. Narrowed: Dropped the 'vs TRx leadership' contrast as a contradiction, because revenue share and TRx share can both be true. Moved the headline from a single quarter (Q2 69.6% to 50.8%) to H1 (74.8% to 50.8%) with class growth captured. Correction: Narrowed finding: in H1 2026 the U.S. ATTR-CM class (Vyndaqel + Amvuttra U.S. + Attruby) grew ~$1.25B (+47%) while U.S. Vyndaqel revenue was flat. Vyndaqel's revenue share fell from ~75% to ~51%. This is revenue share, shaped by price and by Amvuttra's PN use, so it does not contradict Pfizer's TRx-share leadership claim. Pfizer has disclosed share pressure and contracting qualitatively but never sized either.

skeptic_obviousness.round1: refuted=True, major: The competitive share shift is the most-discussed PFE commercial topic, not a hidden one. Analyst Vamil Divan (Guggenheim) asked directly about 'pricing and market share dynamics' for Vyndamax with the new competitors on the 2025Q3 call (PFE:transcripts/2025Q3_transcript.md p8, grade A). Aamir Malik answered on p9: competition is 'taking some first-line share from treatment-naive patients' and Amvuttra has driven 'minimal switching'. A quarter earlier he said 'Attruby is taking some first-line share' and flagged GTN pressure on U.S. Vyndaqel (2025Q2 call p10). Steve Scala asked in 2024Q2 whether competitors would 'take majority share before' LOE (2024Q2 call p17). The rivals publish their own share claims: Alnylam's CCO cites >75% new-patient share in PN and plans to 'replicate' it in CM (ALNY 2026Q1 call p1), and BridgeBio's Jan 2026 deck projects 30-40%+ Attruby share (BBIO:earnings/2026-01-12_ef20062706_ex99-2.md p29). The three revenue lines come from the three companies' own 10-Qs and earnings releases (Vyndaqel U.S. by quarter is in the PFE release product table, PFE:earnings/2026-08-04_pfe-6282026xex99.md p22-23), and ATTR-CM analysts stack them as a matter of course. What is new is only the arithmetic: a revenue-share number of ~51%. It is also partly a price effect that Pfizer already disclosed ('net price erosion... new payer contracts', 10-Q 2026Q2 p38 and release p4), not a pure volume loss. I/B/E/S in the index has no product-level Vyndaqel consensus, so I cannot show the share loss is in numbers. FY2026 revenue consensus ($62.25B) sits inside raised guidance (market/consensus_vs_guidance.csv), so the market is not surprised at the company level. Correction: Narrow it to the gap between Pfizer's 'continued market share leadership' (2025Q3 p9, on a TRx basis) and the revenue view, where the U.S. class lead is down to ~51%. The non-obvious part is the size of the revenue-share drop and that management never quantified it, not the existence of share loss.
skeptic_obviousness.round2: refuted=False, minor. Conceded: Materiality is right that the arithmetic is like for like and that part of the drop is Pfizer's own net price. My round 1 'major, refuted' overweighted the fact that the direction is known; the size is unsaid anywhere I searched. Held: The underlying story (competitors take first-line share, payer contracting cuts net price) is said and answered. Alnylam's 2026Q2 remarks say openly that it is contesting Vyndaqel's leadership. The candidate cannot be sold as a hidden share loss. Narrowed: From 'refuted' to 'held, minor': the only non-obvious content is the ~51% revenue-share figure and its 19-pt drop. Correction: Vyndaqel's share of U.S. ATTR-CM class revenue fell ~19 pts to ~51% in a year (approximate: Amvuttra U.S. includes hATTR-PN, and this is revenue, not patients). No company or analyst in the index has quantified this. Management and rivals have said the direction of share loss and the payer-contract price cuts. Credit it as a quantification, not a discovery.

steps.verdict_reason: In H1 2026 the U.S. ATTR-CM class (Vyndaqel family U.S. + Amvuttra U.S. + Attruby net product revenue) grew about $1.25B (+47%) while U.S. Vyndaqel revenue was flat ($1,975M vs $1,976M), so Vyndaqel's share of U.S. class revenue fell from about 75% to about 51% (Q2 alone: ~70% to ~51%); this is revenue share, shaped by Pfizer's own payer-contract price cuts and by Amvuttra's hATTR-PN use, and Pfizer has never sized it. | Both skeptics re-derived the figures from PFE:10q_2026Q2.md p.38 (U.S. QTD 1,064 vs 990; YTD 1,975 vs 1,976), ALNY:10q_2026Q2.md p.38 (Amvuttra United States QTD 809,079 vs 361,346; YTD 1,511,633 vs 559,310, $000) and BBIO:10q_2026Q2.md p.56 (net product revenue QTD 222,440 vs 71,501; YTD 403,036 vs 108,240); I opened all three pages and confirmed them. H1: 1,975+1,511.6+403.0=3,889.6 vs 1,976+559.3+108.2=2,643.5, +1,246.1 (+47.1%); share 1,975/3,889.6=50.8% vs 1,976/2,643.5=74.8%. Obviousness conceded in round 2 that no PFE, ALNY or BBIO call, release or deck in the index quantifies class revenue share (every share figure is TRx or new-patient starts), after round 1 refuted on the ground that the direction of share loss was said on PFE 2025Q2 call p.10 and 2025Q3 call p.8-9. Materiality conceded the direction is said and dropped the 'contradicts TRx leadership' framing (revenue share and TRx share can both be true). Settled: confirmed as arithmetic, credited as a quantification of a known story, not a discovery. The Q2'25 rival base is a launch trough (Amvuttra's CM label was new), which inflates the swing; the $0.3B/yr shortfall vs FY2025's 8% growth (10-K FY2025 p.44: 3,834 vs 3,547) is a counterfactual, not a decline.

skeptic_materiality.round1: refuted=True, major: Opened policy_gov:policy_gov/cms/cms_fact_sheet_negotiated_prices_ipay2027.md p.2, cms_fact_sheet_selected_list_ipay2028.md p.1, PFE:10k_FY2025.md p.13, p.25, p.44, PFE:10q_2026Q2.md p.35. The CMS figures are on page: MFP $7,871 vs list $15,741 = 50.0%; 2,036.2 x 50% = 1,018. Two math/materiality failures. (1) The 'Medicare = 71% of U.S. net revenue' ratio divides Part D gross covered cost (list basis, before rebates, includes beneficiary cost-sharing) by Pfizer's net U.S. revenue for a different year; it is not a comparable item. The 50% cut is off list, and Ibrance already pays Part D rebates and redesign discounts (10-K p.44), so the net hit is unknown and the $0.3-0.6B range has no anchor. (2) The 10-K patent table (file p.13) lists Ibrance's U.S. basic product patent expiration as 2027, the same year the MFP takes effect. In 2027 Ibrance faces U.S. generic palbociclib, which dwarfs the MFP-vs-rival asymmetry; the 'full year at half price against full-price rivals' framing ignores the larger 2027 event. The selection-date fact stands; the investor-relevant impact does not. Correction: Ibrance's Medicare MFP (50% off list) starts 1 Jan 2027, a year before Kisqali/Verzenio MFPs, but 2027 is also Ibrance's U.S. basic patent expiry year (10-K p.13), so the incremental MFP effect is small next to LOE and cannot be sized from the cited data.

skeptic_obviousness.round1: refuted=True, fatal: Analysts asked this and management answered it directly, and at bottom it is a patent-cliff item. Tim Anderson (BofA) asked on the 2025Q2 call about the Ibrance/Xtandi negotiations for '27 (PFE:companies/PFE/transcripts/2025Q2_transcript.md p13, grade A). Bourla replied: 'Both of them are losing patent on '27 ... the hit on us is very small. The NPV is very small because it's really a few months of exclusivity.' He made the same point in 2024Q1 (call p19: Ibrance and Xtandi 'are approaching their LOE ... the NPV risk ... is not that big'). Pfizer's 10-K lists Ibrance U.S. basic-product expiry as 2027, and the verified LOE calendar has 2027-09-05 (pipeline/loe_calendar.csv IBRANCE US). So the 2027 MFP overlaps U.S. generic entry within the same year. The 'year ahead of Kisqali/Verzenio' asymmetry is mostly moot after September 2027. The MFP itself is a CMS headline (ira_cut_check: 50% verified). 'Zero mentions of Ibrance on the last four calls' is wrong in spirit: Ibrance was discussed in the 2026Q2 release (new HER2+ approval, 2026-08-04 release p7), and Tewari's 2026Q2 CDK4/6 question touched the franchise. Correction: At most: Ibrance's Medicare price drops 50% from 1 Jan 2027, about 8 months before U.S. generics. That is the known, small IRA-before-LOE overlap Bourla already sized as 'very small'.
